extraction.body: Members of Congress are calling on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign, and momentum is building to subpoena the executive, whose company is a leader in advanced artificial intelligence chips. Senate banking committee member Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., doubled down Wednesday on his call for Huang to resign, and a key Democratic House oversight panel member and House Republican piled on. "As a matter of his own conscience, he should resign," Cramer told CNBC, in response to revelations that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy as the chipmaker he co-founded was given permission from the U.S. government to sell its technology to China. Huang, who leads a company that's been a chief beneficiary of the artificial intelligence boom, on Sunday admitted to having an affair with a woman whom news outlets have reported U.S. intelligence concluded was a Chinese spy . The revelation is sending shockwaves through Washington, with lawmakers now fearing that U.S. AI dominance could be at risk. "What bothers me at the end of it is what we don't know is what she knows about him that can be utilized," Cramer said, referring to Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related. "This is a guy that's right now so vulnerable to extortion, blackmail. I just don't think, as a national security matter, we can run the risk." Cramer's comments come on the deadline set by a trio of House lawmakers who requested Huang to testify before their committees on Nov. 18. GOP Reps. Brian Mast, chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, chair of the Permanent Select Committee on China; and Rick Crawford, who leads the House intelligence panel, called for Huang to appear in a Nov. 4 letter . Congress members in the majority party also have subpoena power, should they choose to use it. Mast and Moolenaar told reporters on Wednesday afternoon that they had not yet heard from Huang and that they were giving him until the end of the day to respond. Asked whether the committees were considering subpoenaing Huang if he doesn't agree to appear, Mast said "yes." Moolenaar, when asked the same question, said "all three committees have subpoena power, and I know all three committees have a very serious interest in getting to the bottom of this and having transparency around this." "We are going to continue to pursue this," Moolenaar said. The lawmakers are far from alone in their criticism, concern and outright shock over the affair. And the scrutiny is only expected to intensify with Democrats poised to take over both chambers of Congress in January. Huang has been close with President Donald Trump during the president's second term, traveling on Air Force One to China in May. "Jensen Huang should resign from Nvidia," Rep. Suhas Subramanyam, D-Va., a member of the House Oversight Committee, told CNBC. Subramanyam is the top Democrat on the panel's Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs. "I didn't agree with his sentiment that there's no downside to exporting chips to China," he said. "But I never thought that he might be having an affair with a Chinese spy who was helping smuggle chips into China at an alarming rate." Rep. Don Bacon , R-Neb., who is retiring from Congress after sometimes bucking Trump, also said the CEO should step down. "From the little I know, yes." Bacon told CNBC in response to whether Huang should resign. "I mean, he allowed himself to get compromised by the Chinese government. Not good." Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with China hawks on Capitol Hill. Democrats are widely expected to launch myriad investigations into the White House and industry when they assume control of both chambers of Congress in January. Nvidia is now likely to be at the center of those probes. "There's two parts to this investigation that [need] to happen somewhere immediately," Subramanyam said. "One is what was going on with Nvidia and China, and two is why the administration did nothing about it even though they appeared to have known, and what the administration knew, and what influence the money from Nvidia and Jensen Huang had on this administration, essentially staying silent." Rep. Jay Obernolte , R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, said Tuesday he hopes that the Huang scandal can avoid becoming a distraction in talks about imposing export controls on advanced AI chips. The situation may give Congress additional ammunition as it tries to pass a suite of bills in this year's National Defense Authorization Act to tighten export controls on advanced AI chips. Congress has still not passed the annual defense bill, which is a top priority for lawmakers in the lame-duck session. Those bills include the AI Overwatch Act , the MATCH Act and the Chip Security Act — all of which are aimed at preventing U.S. chip technology from falling into adversarial hands. Sens. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., and Jim Banks, R-Ind., in a statement following the revelation of Huang's affair, urged their colleagues to include the AI Overwatch Act. Warren, the incoming Senate banking committee chair, sponsored the bill in the Senate with Banks. "Huang's confirmation of a relationship with a suspected spy for China's intelligence service makes these national security concerns even more urgent and raises important questions NVIDIA must answer about the extent to which these activities were related," the senators said. "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips." And Subramanyam warned that what Nvidia does now — and whether Huang remains atop the company — could affect its relationship with Washington and whether lawmakers crack down. "If Nvidia finds out that he knew about what was going on and does nothing about it, then Nvidia is making a choice and us as regulators and as watchdogs need to defend the American people," he said. US HOUSE Speaker Mike Johnson said on Thursday (Nov 12) there was growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China after a spy scandal forced out Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang stepped down after reports of a romantic relationship with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government.

Lawmakers from both parties have since called for tougher restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips, threatening access to chips that underpin China’s surging AI development. And senior White House officials were discussing whether Commerce ​Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington.

A growing number of lawmakers have criticised Lutnick for the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia’s exports to China.

Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems. The US has sought for years to limit China’s access to Nvidia’s chips because it does not want the Chinese military to benefit from them.

“The export controls on chips to China has been a big issue around here,” Johnson, a Louisiana Republican, told reporters at the US Capitol, adding he favoured limiting China’s access to the advanced technology. “I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.”

The Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia partner the US government suspects of helping China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.
The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.

Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent ​Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company’s chips remotely.

Congressional Republicans are keen to attach new restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China in the annual defence authorisation Bill, a must-pass measure that funds the military and typically ​attracts bipartisan support, according to a Senate aide, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

Lawmakers are pressing their colleagues to pass at least four Bills on chip exports, according to statements since Monday. The AI Overwatch Act would give Congress more power over advanced AI chip exports. The Chip Security Act would require ​companies to track the location of advanced AI processors to prevent smuggling.

The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China. The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips.

Huang’s resignation is unlikely to end congressional scrutiny of Nvidia and could leave the former chief executive more exposed to investigation, said Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation.
“Congress can still subpoena him and Nvidia should conduct an independent investigation to determine whether the problems extend beyond Huang,” Cheung said.

Cheung said Huang’s departure could weaken Nvidia’s influence in Washington and create additional momentum for legislation that tightens restrictions on advanced chip exports. He said Nvidia’s new leadership could also reconsider the company’s China strategy as it seeks to rebuild trust with US policymakers.

Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26. House Foreign Affairs chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.
Mast and two other leading House Republicans asked Huang last week to brief them behind closed doors about his relationship with Alice Huang. REUTERS

NEW YORK, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Congress is more likely to pass legislation aimed at tightening China's access to AI chips in light of news that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected ‌Chinese intelligence agent, lawmakers and advocates said.
Three chip-related measures are slated for possible inclusion in the annual defense authorization ‌bill for fiscal year 2027, which began in October.

"The hurdle these bills ‌need to clear is getting the White House onboard," said ​Chris MacKenzie, a spokesman for Americans ​for Responsible Innovation, a Washington nonprofit organization that favors the measures.
In March, the senators had urged the Department of Commerce to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses to China and conduct a full security review.
They added: "It is time for Congress to take decisive action to pass key bills like the AI Overwatch Act in the NDAA that will cut off pathways through which China accesses advanced chips."
Until the US Department of Justice brought indictments tied to chip smuggling last year, Huang and Nvidia had argued there was no such smuggling.
The ⁠company said it complied with export laws.
Nvidia is considered the biggest opponent of both the Chip Security and AI Overwatch ‌acts, according to one former congressional staffer ⁠who had direct contact with the company over several months.
"Congress has the tools to prevent powerful AI chips from getting in the wrong hands and posing a ‌national security risk," Foster posted on X on Monday, in response to ​news of Huang's affair.

The Information Technology Industry ‌Council, whose members include Nvidia, among other groups, has opposed the measures, arguing they could undermine US competitiveness and ​complicate export control policy.
A spokeswoman for the council declined comment on the current Nvidia situation.
Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips.
Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.
Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.
While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters.
Nvidia’s advanced AI chips are widely used to develop cutting-edge AI models, making the company key to the US race against China to build superior AI systems.
“I think there’s a developing consensus in Congress that is an important position to take.”

And senior White House officials were discussing whether Commerce ​Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington.
The Match Act would pressure US allies to restrict sales and maintenance of advanced chipmaking equipment destined for China.
The Remote Access Security Act would give the Commerce Department the tools to stop Chinese firms from renting overseas data centres to access Nvidia chips.

Reuters reported that Chinese AI companies are trying to rent ​Nvidia-powered computing capacity outside China because they are worried the Jensen Huang allegations could spur Washington to tighten restrictions on their ability to access the company’s chips remotely.

A growing number of lawmakers have criticised Lutnick for the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia’s exports to China.
Cheung said Huang’s departure could weaken Nvidia’s influence in Washington and create additional momentum for legislation that tightens restrictions on advanced chip exports.

Jensen Huang is separately expected to testify before Congress before Thanksgiving, which falls on Nov 26.
House Foreign Affairs chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, told reporters on Thursday that congressional staff spoke with Nvidia on Wednesday night about a date and location for his testimony.

Huang’s resignation is unlikely to end congressional scrutiny of Nvidia and could leave the former chief executive more exposed to investigation, said Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation.
The case has revived claims among China critics in Washington that US export policies are too weak, boosting calls for more restrictions.

passages: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple will announce its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027, with shipments before the end of next year.
Gurman says the first model won’t have augmented reality features.
Apple hasn’t announced a price, battery spec, or final name, and no source gives Gulf availability.
According to Bloomberg, Apple wants its App Store developers to help it compete with market leader Meta and its Ray-Ban glasses.
Samsung has confirmed its own AR glasses for 2026, as Tbreak reported .
The glasses have Wi-Fi, so certain functions outside third-party apps keep working when the iPhone isn’t nearby.
Apple is also stressing sound quality, which employees have called industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music, and FaceTime audio.
Employees reportedly describe the product as “AirPods for your face”; camera-equipped AirPods are a separate product.
According to The Verge , the newly revamped Siri AI, with its fine-grained control over apps, is key to the glasses’ success.
The prototypes, codenamed N50, run a pared-down version of visionOS on a new processor based on Apple’s older smartwatch chips.
A MagSafe-like charger, roughly the size of a Tic Tac, works while the glasses are worn.
MacRumors reported in July that Gurman expects privacy to be a focus.
Gurman reports Apple envisions restaurant reservations through OpenTable, rides through Uber or Lyft, Starbucks orders, Amazon shopping, and Fandango tickets.
Built-in functions cover Visual Intelligence, notifications, messages, calendar, reminders, music, and smart home control.
According to Digital Trends, software is running behind, though the June reveal and year-end shipping are still in place and much of the hardware is largely finalised.

extraction.body: Apple’s smart glasses are among the worst-kept secrets in the tech world. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says the company’s first model, which will lack augmented reality features, will be announced at June’s WWDC next year. They likely won’t ship right away, however, with Gurman saying only that “glasses shipments would begin before the end of the year.” Key to their success will be the newly revamped Siri AI, which is adding fine-grained control over apps. By adding those features now and letting developers add support on the iPhone first, it’s hoping that its smart glasses will be able to hit the ground running. They also have a MagSafe-like charger Gurman describes as “flat, rectangular” and “roughly the size of a Tic Tac,” which can be used even while still wearing the glasses. In addition to Apple putting an emphasis on style, privacy, and audio quality, the company is also hoping that Wi-Fi connectivity will grant them a certain amount of freedom, despite relying on an iPhone to actually execute many tasks: > The glasses have Wi-Fi, allowing certain functions outside of third-party apps to continue working when the iPhone isn’t nearby. Users could theoretically keep listening to audio over Wi-Fi after walking away from their phones, for instance, though the eyewear won’t operate as a fully independent device. Apple is also emphasizing the sound quality, which employees have said is industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music playback and FaceTime audio communication.

passages: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple will announce its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027, with shipments before the end of next year.
Gurman says the first model won’t have augmented reality features.
Apple hasn’t announced a price, battery spec, or final name, and no source gives Gulf availability.
According to Bloomberg, Apple wants its App Store developers to help it compete with market leader Meta and its Ray-Ban glasses.
Samsung has confirmed its own AR glasses for 2026, as Tbreak reported .
The glasses have Wi-Fi, so certain functions outside third-party apps keep working when the iPhone isn’t nearby.
Apple is also stressing sound quality, which employees have called industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music, and FaceTime audio.
Employees reportedly describe the product as “AirPods for your face”; camera-equipped AirPods are a separate product.
According to The Verge , the newly revamped Siri AI, with its fine-grained control over apps, is key to the glasses’ success.
The prototypes, codenamed N50, run a pared-down version of visionOS on a new processor based on Apple’s older smartwatch chips.
A MagSafe-like charger, roughly the size of a Tic Tac, works while the glasses are worn.
MacRumors reported in July that Gurman expects privacy to be a focus.
Gurman reports Apple envisions restaurant reservations through OpenTable, rides through Uber or Lyft, Starbucks orders, Amazon shopping, and Fandango tickets.
Built-in functions cover Visual Intelligence, notifications, messages, calendar, reminders, music, and smart home control.
According to Digital Trends, software is running behind, though the June reveal and year-end shipping are still in place and much of the hardware is largely finalised.

The chip is reportedly derived from older Apple Watch processors. Wi-Fi keeps some functions, such as audio, working without an iPhone nearby. story.title: Apple’s first smart glasses are coming together

facts.text: As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses.
They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world.
Michael is a 9to5Mac Reporter, leading all of our Apple news coverage on weekends and reviewing the newest Apple products and accessories.
He got started in the world of Apple news during the pandemic, and it became a growing hobby.
He’s also an indie iOS developer, and started the weekly Indie App Spotlight series, which has covered hundreds of blooming new apps since it launched.
In his free time, he enjoys shooting street photography around New York City on his Sony A7RV.
Beyond that, it’s unclear how Apple will make these useful for health – just don’t expect it in the first iteration.
Unlike Meta, Apple isn’t partnering with an existing eyewear-maker to design these glasses.
According to Bloomberg , the company is instead designing them in house, with a number of different styles in the works:
On the other hand, though – they might not allow for the glasses to take photos and videos normally, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.
Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses have become a massive privacy concern lately, and Apple may want to avoid that.
They’re supposedly going to be made of acetate, a more durable and higher-end alternative to plastic.
Apple will also offer them in a few finishes, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.
In a future iteration of the product, Apple is reportedly considering positioning the product as a health device.
Check out 9to5Mac on YouTube for more Apple news:

Featuring two built in cables, a built in display, multiple ports, a 25,000mAh capacity, and up to 100W of output - this is one of the best battery banks for recharging your entire Apple ecosystem on the go.
Another feature that we’ll likely see on these glasses is the ability for you to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you later, as we first saw in the macOS 26.7 leak .
Some of my favorite Apple accessory recommendations:
First and foremost, these glasses are AI glasses, not AR glasses.
Apple’s smart glasses are among the worst-kept secrets in the tech world.
By adding those features now and letting developers add support on the iPhone first, it’s hoping that its smart glasses will be able to hit the ground running.
Apple is also emphasizing the sound quality, which employees have said is industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music playback and FaceTime audio communication.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple will announce its first smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027, with shipments before the end of next year.
Gurman says the first model won’t have augmented reality features.
Apple hasn’t announced a price, battery spec, or final name, and no source gives Gulf availability.
According to Bloomberg, Apple wants its App Store developers to help it compete with market leader Meta and its Ray-Ban glasses.
Samsung has confirmed its own AR glasses for 2026, as Tbreak reported .
The glasses have Wi-Fi, so certain functions outside third-party apps keep working when the iPhone isn’t nearby.
Apple is also stressing sound quality, which employees have called industry-leading, with support for phone calls, music, and FaceTime audio.
Employees reportedly describe the product as “AirPods for your face”; camera-equipped AirPods are a separate product.
According to The Verge , the newly revamped Siri AI, with its fine-grained control over apps, is key to the glasses’ success.
The prototypes, codenamed N50, run a pared-down version of visionOS on a new processor based on Apple’s older smartwatch chips.
A MagSafe-like charger, roughly the size of a Tic Tac, works while the glasses are worn.
MacRumors reported in July that Gurman expects privacy to be a focus.
Gurman reports Apple envisions restaurant reservations through OpenTable, rides through Uber or Lyft, Starbucks orders, Amazon shopping, and Fandango tickets.
Built-in functions cover Visual Intelligence, notifications, messages, calendar, reminders, music, and smart home control.
According to Digital Trends, software is running behind, though the June reveal and year-end shipping are still in place and much of the hardware is largely finalised.

For Android owners, the iPhone requirement is the key detail.
That leaves Android users with options like Meta’s Ray-Ban line and Google and Samsung’s Android XR glasses, which start at $395 .
Siri’s app-action controls arrived in the first iOS 27.3 beta, per the report.
It fits with earlier reporting that Siri could become an AI agent that acts inside apps for you.
Plans can change before a 2027 launch, so this isn’t a final word on Android compatibility.

passages: Now, two prominent hedge fund managers , Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management, are calling for the board to consider bringing back Huang.

In a letter to the board, the two investors asked the directors "to pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang." They added, "The Founder and longtime incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known."
At this point, Huang's return seems like a long shot and is not a reason to buy the stock.
Bringing him back could lead to further chaos at the company, especially while Nvidia is being investigated by regulators.
Jensen Huang's departure has shocked the business world and left Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) investors wondering what happens next.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
It could take months and multiple investigations to determine if Jensen Huang or Nvidia broke any laws or what, if anything, may have been leaked to Alice Huang.
Jensen Huang speaking on stage. Image source: Getty Images.
At minimum, for Huang to return, there would need to be a full exoneration by the federal government over the chip export ordeal, and that will take time.
Prior to the recent slide, Nvidia had added roughly $5 trillion in market value over the last decade, and its investors don't want to see that continue to erode.

Nvidia announced Huang's resignation Thursday morning after meeting the night before to reportedly oust him, and it's not clear if Huang willingly agreed to walk away in the end, or if he was pushed out.
Shares of the AI chip leader tumbled 15% last week as the drama unfolded around Huang, and are down a third from their peak in October.

Prior to the recent slide, Nvidia had added roughly $5 trillion in market value over the last decade, and its investors don't want to see that continue to erode. Now, two prominent hedge fund managers , Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management, are calling for the board to consider bringing back Huang. In a letter to the board, the two investors asked the directors "to pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future of Nvidia that leaves all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang." They added, "The Founder and longtime incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known." Jensen Huang speaking on stage. Image source: Getty Images. In addition to that letter, an open petition that calls for him to be reinstated has received more than 80,000 signatures, and hundreds of Nvidia employees have signed a letter calling for Huang to be brought back. Clearly, there's a strong interest in his return. This call comes at the same time that the federal government said that it has not determined that Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive with whom Jensen Huang had an affair, is a spy. In other words, she was not directly employed by Beijing and may instead have been an "asset," someone who could have passed along information to Chinese intelligence. It could take months and multiple investigations to determine if Jensen Huang or Nvidia broke any laws or what, if anything, may have been leaked to Alice Huang. At minimum, for Huang to return, there would need to be a full exoneration by the federal government over the chip export ordeal, and that will take time. Jensen has agreed to testify before Congress. According to Bloomberg , Huang seemed to express remorse before he resigned, saying, "I'm a piece of sh--." The episode has been humiliating for him, and the resignation may have come to avoid more dirty laundry being aired in the media. After the resignation, Reuters reported a third affair with an unnamed employee, and there could be more. In other words, it's unclear if Huang wants his job back right now. At this point, Huang's return seems like a long shot and is not a reason to buy the stock. Bringing him back could lead to further chaos at the company, especially while Nvidia is being investigated by regulators. The calls could grow louder, though, depending on how the company performs without him, and if enough shareholders want him back, they could install a new board to do so. Rather than indulging in that drama, investors are better off focusing on the facts on the ground and what they mean for the future of Nvidia. We'll get more insights when the company reports third-quarter earnings on Tuesday during the earnings call. How CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress handles the call and what information she shares should help signal where the company goes from here. extraction.body: Just three days after the high-profile resignation of the founder of the world's most valuable chipmaker, his supporters in Silicon Valley have set up a dedicated war room to pressure the board of directors. However, regaining the seat will not be easy for the billionaire: he does not hold a controlling stake, while the corporation is already scouting for his replacement and bracing for scrutiny from Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Thursday, November 12, following the exposure of extramarital relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct subordinate, is already discussing a plan to return to the company with his confidants. This was reported on Sunday, November 15, by the British newspaper Financial Times. According to an associate of the businessman, Silicon Valley top executives have formed a dedicated "war room" to lobby Nvidia's board of directors for Huang's reinstatement, as well as to try to secure support in the White House. "Everyone who matters in tech outside of the frontier labs loves Jensen," said an interlocutor of the publication, adding that these efforts have the backing of the former CEO himself. Over the weekend, the public campaign for the return of the founder of the $4 trillion corporation gained momentum. An open letter to the board of directors demanding to "Bring Jensen Back" was supported by Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, as well as several Nvidia employees. Back on Friday, major shareholders of the company—Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management head Gavin Baker—published an appeal to the corporate leadership, urging them to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," given his decades of service and the uncertainty surrounding the future of the business. Despite pressure from billionaires and investors, the push to rehabilitate Huang faces severe legal and political obstacles. Unlike many other tech titan founders, Huang does not hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and therefore cannot veto decisions made by the board of directors. The board itself is currently conducting an independent investigation into the former chief's conduct. Even those in the businessman's camp acknowledge the weakness of his position. "An affair with a subordinate is a firing offense," admitted one member of Huang's support group. Aside from the internal workplace affair with Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, Huang's primary problem stems from his connection to Alice Huang, head of the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which US authorities suspect of espionage and smuggling chips into China. This episode has drawn intense scrutiny toward how Nvidia monitors the sales of its artificial intelligence processors to clients in Asia. On Sunday, November 15, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly called for a "radical refresh" in Nvidia's leadership following the departure of its founder. Meanwhile, the corporation's interim CEO Colette Kress is preparing the company for the release of its quarterly financial report on Tuesday, while the board of directors is already looking for a permanent successor. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia representatives have approached Rene Haas, CEO of the British processor architecture designer Arm Holdings, with an offer to head the corporation, though officially the company states that a formal process to select a new leader has not yet been launched. Representatives of Nvidia and Jensen Huang himself declined to comment on his potential return.

extraction.body: Just three days after the high-profile resignation of the founder of the world's most valuable chipmaker, his supporters in Silicon Valley have set up a dedicated war room to pressure the board of directors. However, regaining the seat will not be easy for the billionaire: he does not hold a controlling stake, while the corporation is already scouting for his replacement and bracing for scrutiny from Washington. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned on Thursday, November 12, following the exposure of extramarital relationships with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct subordinate, is already discussing a plan to return to the company with his confidants. This was reported on Sunday, November 15, by the British newspaper Financial Times. According to an associate of the businessman, Silicon Valley top executives have formed a dedicated "war room" to lobby Nvidia's board of directors for Huang's reinstatement, as well as to try to secure support in the White House. "Everyone who matters in tech outside of the frontier labs loves Jensen," said an interlocutor of the publication, adding that these efforts have the backing of the former CEO himself. Over the weekend, the public campaign for the return of the founder of the $4 trillion corporation gained momentum. An open letter to the board of directors demanding to "Bring Jensen Back" was supported by Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, as well as several Nvidia employees. Back on Friday, major shareholders of the company—Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management head Gavin Baker—published an appeal to the corporate leadership, urging them to keep "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang," given his decades of service and the uncertainty surrounding the future of the business. Despite pressure from billionaires and investors, the push to rehabilitate Huang faces severe legal and political obstacles. Unlike many other tech titan founders, Huang does not hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and therefore cannot veto decisions made by the board of directors. The board itself is currently conducting an independent investigation into the former chief's conduct. Even those in the businessman's camp acknowledge the weakness of his position. "An affair with a subordinate is a firing offense," admitted one member of Huang's support group. Aside from the internal workplace affair with Vice President of Healthcare Kimberly Powell, Huang's primary problem stems from his connection to Alice Huang, head of the Singapore-based company Megaspeed, which US authorities suspect of espionage and smuggling chips into China. This episode has drawn intense scrutiny toward how Nvidia monitors the sales of its artificial intelligence processors to clients in Asia. On Sunday, November 15, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly called for a "radical refresh" in Nvidia's leadership following the departure of its founder. Meanwhile, the corporation's interim CEO Colette Kress is preparing the company for the release of its quarterly financial report on Tuesday, while the board of directors is already looking for a permanent successor. According to the Financial Times, Nvidia representatives have approached Rene Haas, CEO of the British processor architecture designer Arm Holdings, with an offer to head the corporation, though officially the company states that a formal process to select a new leader has not yet been launched. Representatives of Nvidia and Jensen Huang himself declined to comment on his potential return.

passages: The United Nations has launched new global priorities at COP31 to ensure that artificial intelligence (AI) provides reliable information on climate change and promotes transparency about its environmental impact.
They require AI companies to assess how their systems affect climate information integrity and publish the findings.
Governments are expected to integrate information integrity into their national AI strategies and climate plans.

Beyond the use of AI, the initiative also seeks to address the role of digital advertising in spreading climate disinformation as the advertising supply chain lacks transparency, making it difficult for brands to know who and what their money funds, including climate disinformation.

Antalya, Nov 13 (SocialNews.XYZ) At COP31, the Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change on Friday launched the Priorities for Action on AI for Climate Information Integrity, setting out what states, AI actors, advertisers, researchers, journalists and funders can do so that people can rely on climate information from AI, and about it.

The priorities, put forward by Global Initiative co-chairs Brazil, the UN and UNESCO, target two sides of one AI information gap: the reliability of the climate information people receive from AI, and the reliability of information about AI’s own impact on the climate.
More and more people are turning to AI for climate information, yet the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI warns that “producing fluent text is easier than producing factual text”.
The risks can heighten during climate disasters, when AI-generated images and videos can spread faster than oﬃcial warnings.

Meanwhile, the public is asked to accept claims about AI’s own climate impact without the necessary data to judge. Building on the Belém Declaration and the UN Global Principles for Information Integrity, the Priorities rest on transparency, accountability and human rights.
For AI companies, this means assessing how their systems affect climate information integrity and publishing the findings, and disclosing their energy use and carbon, water and land footprints.
Actions for states include integrating information integrity into national AI strategies and climate plans.

Global Advertising Charter says: follow the money. Advertising is the dominant business model of the digital information ecosystem. Yet because the advertising supply chain is opaque, brands often cannot tell who and what their money funds, including climate disinformation.

To change that, the Charter for Climate Information Integrity in Advertising, launched by Conscious Advertising Network (CAN) and Climate Action Against Disinformation (CAAD) and supported by the Global Initiative, calls for transparency across the advertising supply chain to ensure advertisers have visibility of advertising placement while respecting user privacy.

The charter also calls for verification of all advertisers on digital platforms, action on greenwashing and ensuring advertising actors publicly disclose their relationships with fossil fuel actors. Strengthening information integrity requires resources.

At COP31, the Global Initiative called for new investment in the information people rely on to understand and act on climate change. Germany answered the call, committing EUR 2 million to the Global Fund for Information Integrity on Climate Change, administered by UNESCO, for grants to support research, develop communication strategies and undertake public awareness campaigns.

The Initiative urged other countries to invest in the Fund. Political momentum grows. One year after information integrity entered a COP (Conference of the Parties) outcome decision for the first time, at COP30 in Belém, 29 countries and the European Union have now signed and are implementing the Belém Declaration on Information Integrity on Climate Change, which remains open for endorsement.

A new initiative to ensure the reliability of climate information generated by artificial intelligence is being launched by the Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change. The Priorities for Action on AI and Climate Information Integrity, which is set to be launched at COP31 on 13 November, follows on from a warning by the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI that as more people turn to chatbots for climate information, ‘producing fluent text is easier than producing factual text’. The priorities will seek to set out measures that governments, AI actors, advertisers, researchers, journalists and other related parties can do to ensure climate information on AI is trustworthy. A separate initiative, the Charter for Climate Information Integrity in Advertising , will be launched on 14 November, which calls on advertisers, advertising agencies and digital platforms to stop funding climate disinformation. Both initiatives follow on from progress made at COP30, where information integrity entered a COP outcome decision for the first time – the Belém Declaration on Information Integrity on Climate Change. To date, 29 countries, along with the European Union, have committed to the declaration. The Global Initiative will also hold two pavilion sessions on the topic – on 14 November, the SDG Pavilion will host a discussion on the relationship between climate information integrity and delivery of the Sustainable Development Goals, subtitled ‘From Words To Action’. This will be followed by a session at the UN Pavilion on 16 November, which will examine what effective policy looks like in practice. The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change was launched by the Government of Brazil, the United Nations and UNESCO at the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Rio de Janeiro, which took place in November 2024. It brings together governments, international organisations and civil society to strengthen research and action on climate information integrity. The Global Fund for Information Integrity on Climate Change also falls under its remit. Read more here .

sources.title: At COP31, Turkey pushes zero-waste plan to curb climate change - WSLS
passages: ANTALYA – As world leaders gathered for United Nations climate talks in the Turkish resort town of Antalya on Wednesday, host Turkey urged countries to commit to a zero-waste initiative aimed at reducing emissions and helping get global efforts to curb climate change back on track.

“Recovered materials can be cheaper when reliable supplies, efficient processing and nearby demand outweigh the costs of collection, sorting and transport,” said Samed Agirbas, president of the nonprofit Zero Waste Foundation and a COP31 high-level climate champion.
It definitely needs to be supported with concrete measures and further action,” said Berk Butan, who heads the waste campaign for Greenpeace Turkey.
Turkey is also the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste, according to nonprofit emissions tracker Climate TRACE.
“We’ll not stop here and we will continue working and making every effort until we achieve the goal of zero waste."

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan touted his country's progress on recycling, saying its rate had risen from about 13% in 2017, when the zero waste movement began, to about 40% by the end of 2025.
Conference agreements are often nonbinding and past hosts have been criticized for failing to follow through on promises.
Turkey also faces scrutiny over its own climate record.

(AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana, File) ANTALYA – As world leaders gathered for United Nations climate talks in the Turkish resort town of Antalya on Wednesday, host Turkey urged countries to commit to a zero-waste initiative aimed at reducing emissions and helping get global efforts to curb climate change back on track. "Some 90 million tons of waste have been brought back into our economy,” Erdogan told the leaders' summit. “We’ll not stop here and we will continue working and making every effort until we achieve the goal of zero waste." Turkey has outlined 10 priorities for this year’s climate talks, known as COP31 , with a pledge to accelerate electrification and the zero-waste initiatives emerging as major talking points during the opening days of the conference. Turkish first lady Emine Erdogan, who attended Wednesday's talks, has been a driving force behind the zero-waste initiative, which aims to reduce methane emissions, cut food waste and promote a circular economy in which materials are reused and recycled. “Recovered materials can be cheaper when reliable supplies, efficient processing and nearby demand outweigh the costs of collection, sorting and transport,” said Samed Agirbas, president of the nonprofit Zero Waste Foundation and a COP31 high-level climate champion. If implemented, energy experts say the initiatives could slow global warming and reduce the environmental footprint of renewable energy technologies, like solar panels and batteries. But there is still a risk these climate ambitions may fall flat. Conference agreements are often nonbinding and past hosts have been criticized for failing to follow through on promises. Turkey also faces scrutiny over its own climate record. “The Zero Waste target is a good target. It definitely needs to be supported with concrete measures and further action,” said Berk Butan, who heads the waste campaign for Greenpeace Turkey. “But fundamentally, we also need to recognize its shortcomings.” As the second biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide, the reduction of methane emissions could significantly slow global warming, according to the U.N. During the first three days of the climate talks, leaders repeatedly called for urgent climate action. The U.N. recently had to readjust a decades-old goal of limiting the rise of global temperatures because the world was blowing past previous thresholds. While Turkey wants countries to commit to reducing methane emissions, it has not signed the Global Methane Pledge. Launched at the 2021 climate talks in Glasgow, the initiative aims to reduce methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030. Turkey is also the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste, according to nonprofit emissions tracker Climate TRACE. “Methane emissions from waste disposal are an important challenge,” said Agirbas, with the Zero Waste Foundation. Circular economy may dent emissions, but challenges remain A circular economy — an economic model that generally prioritizes recycling and other regenerative approaches that create less waste— would help reduce emissions, but not every country has the resources to take such steps. Ke Wang, an energy expert at the WRI's Polsky Center for the Global Energy Transition, said that this is “a vital strategy for cutting greenhouse gas emissions." But recycling food waste is difficult because it decomposes quickly, making separation and processing expensive. Collecting and transporting wet, smelly food waste also requires specialized logistics and infrastructure that many countries lack. “Waste and food loss account for almost 10% of total emissions, so we need to integrate these actions,” Adalberto Maluf, a top official in Brazil’s environment ministry, told The Associated Press. The recycling of already-mined materials is key to reducing the reliance on mining, according to experts, which will only become more important as the world relies more on critical mineral-dependent renewable technologies. The International Energy Agency estimates that scaling up recycling could lower the need for new mining by between 25% and 40% by 2050. Most countries don’t recycle critical materials because it’s cheaper to mine them. The technology and infrastructure needed to recycle these materials are also concentrated in a handful of nations, like China. The European Union and the U.S. will likely only have the capacity to recycle 30% of their raw materials by 2040, according to the IEA. “We must do a better job with our materials retrieval, reuse and recycling,” said Aimee Boulanger, executive director of the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance. She stressed the need to create incentives for “retrieving the materials, taking things apart, being able to reuse them again in a circular way.” Arasu reported from Bengaluru, India, Milko from Islamabad, Pakistan and Delgado from Bangkok. coreStoryFacts.text: The United Nations has launched new global priorities at COP31 to ensure that artificial intelligence (AI) provides reliable information on climate change and promotes transparency about its environmental impact.
They require AI companies to assess how their systems affect climate information integrity and publish the findings.
Governments are expected to integrate information integrity into their national AI strategies and climate plans.
Home » General » Environment » COP31: New global priorities target role of AI in climate information integrity
At COP31, the Global Initiative called for new investment in the information people rely on to understand and act on climate change.
Building on the Belém Declaration and the UN Global Principles for Information Integrity, the Priorities rest on transparency, accountability and human rights.
Actions for states include integrating information integrity into national AI strategies and climate plans.
More and more people are turning to AI for climate information, yet the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI warns that “producing fluent text is easier than producing factual text”.
Strengthening information integrity requires resources.

A separate initiative, the Charter for Climate Information Integrity in Advertising , will be launched on 14 November, which calls on advertisers, advertising agencies and digital platforms to stop funding climate disinformation.

The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change was launched by the Government of Brazil, the United Nations and UNESCO at the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Rio de Janeiro, which took place in November 2024.
The priorities will seek to set out measures that governments, AI actors, advertisers, researchers, journalists and other related parties can do to ensure climate information on AI is trustworthy.

A new initiative to ensure the reliability of climate information generated by artificial intelligence is being launched by the Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change. The Priorities for Action on AI and Climate Information Integrity, which is set to be launched at COP31 on 13 November, follows on from a warning by the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI that as more people turn to chatbots for climate information, ‘producing fluent text is easier than producing factual text’. The priorities will seek to set out measures that governments, AI actors, advertisers, researchers, journalists and other related parties can do to ensure climate information on AI is trustworthy. A separate initiative, the Charter for Climate Information Integrity in Advertising , will be launched on 14 November, which calls on advertisers, advertising agencies and digital platforms to stop funding climate disinformation. Both initiatives follow on from progress made at COP30, where information integrity entered a COP outcome decision for the first time – the Belém Declaration on Information Integrity on Climate Change. To date, 29 countries, along with the European Union, have committed to the declaration. The Global Initiative will also hold two pavilion sessions on the topic – on 14 November, the SDG Pavilion will host a discussion on the relationship between climate information integrity and delivery of the Sustainable Development Goals, subtitled ‘From Words To Action’. This will be followed by a session at the UN Pavilion on 16 November, which will examine what effective policy looks like in practice. The Global Initiative for Information Integrity on Climate Change was launched by the Government of Brazil, the United Nations and UNESCO at the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Rio de Janeiro, which took place in November 2024. It brings together governments, international organisations and civil society to strengthen research and action on climate information integrity. The Global Fund for Information Integrity on Climate Change also falls under its remit. Read more here .

(AP Photo/Tatan Syuflana, File) ANTALYA – As world leaders gathered for United Nations climate talks in the Turkish resort town of Antalya on Wednesday, host Turkey urged countries to commit to a zero-waste initiative aimed at reducing emissions and helping get global efforts to curb climate change back on track. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan touted his country's progress on recycling, saying its rate had risen from about 13% in 2017, when the zero waste movement began, to about 40% by the end of 2025. "Some 90 million tons of waste have been brought back into our economy,” Erdogan told the leaders' summit. “We’ll not stop here and we will continue working and making every effort until we achieve the goal of zero waste." Turkey has outlined 10 priorities for this year’s climate talks, known as COP31 , with a pledge to accelerate electrification and the zero-waste initiatives emerging as major talking points during the opening days of the conference. Turkish first lady Emine Erdogan, who attended Wednesday's talks, has been a driving force behind the zero-waste initiative, which aims to reduce methane emissions, cut food waste and promote a circular economy in which materials are reused and recycled. “Recovered materials can be cheaper when reliable supplies, efficient processing and nearby demand outweigh the costs of collection, sorting and transport,” said Samed Agirbas, president of the nonprofit Zero Waste Foundation and a COP31 high-level climate champion. If implemented, energy experts say the initiatives could slow global warming and reduce the environmental footprint of renewable energy technologies, like solar panels and batteries. But there is still a risk these climate ambitions may fall flat. Conference agreements are often nonbinding and past hosts have been criticized for failing to follow through on promises. Turkey also faces scrutiny over its own climate record. “The Zero Waste target is a good target. It definitely needs to be supported with concrete measures and further action,” said Berk Butan, who heads the waste campaign for Greenpeace Turkey. “But fundamentally, we also need to recognize its shortcomings.” As the second biggest cause of climate change after carbon dioxide, the reduction of methane emissions could significantly slow global warming, according to the U.N. During the first three days of the climate talks, leaders repeatedly called for urgent climate action. The U.N. recently had to readjust a decades-old goal of limiting the rise of global temperatures because the world was blowing past previous thresholds. While Turkey wants countries to commit to reducing methane emissions, it has not signed the Global Methane Pledge. Launched at the 2021 climate talks in Glasgow, the initiative aims to reduce methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030. Turkey is also the world’s fifth-biggest emitter of methane from solid waste, according to nonprofit emissions tracker Climate TRACE. “Methane emissions from waste disposal are an important challenge,” said Agirbas, with the Zero Waste Foundation. Circular economy may dent emissions, but challenges remain A circular economy — an economic model that generally prioritizes recycling and other regenerative approaches that create less waste— would help reduce emissions, but not every country has the resources to take such steps. Ke Wang, an energy expert at the WRI's Polsky Center for the Global Energy Transition, said that this is “a vital strategy for cutting greenhouse gas emissions." But recycling food waste is difficult because it decomposes quickly, making separation and processing expensive. Collecting and transporting wet, smelly food waste also requires specialized logistics and infrastructure that many countries lack. “Waste and food loss account for almost 10% of total emissions, so we need to integrate these actions,” Adalberto Maluf, a top official in Brazil’s environment ministry, told The Associated Press. The recycling of already-mined materials is key to reducing the reliance on mining, according to experts, which will only become more important as the world relies more on critical mineral-dependent renewable technologies. The International Energy Agency estimates that scaling up recycling could lower the need for new mining by between 25% and 40% by 2050. Most countries don’t recycle critical materials because it’s cheaper to mine them. The technology and infrastructure needed to recycle these materials are also concentrated in a handful of nations, like China. The European Union and the U.S. will likely only have the capacity to recycle 30% of their raw materials by 2040, according to the IEA. “We must do a better job with our materials retrieval, reuse and recycling,” said Aimee Boulanger, executive director of the Initiative for Responsible Mining Assurance. She stressed the need to create incentives for “retrieving the materials, taking things apart, being able to reuse them again in a circular way.” Arasu reported from Bengaluru, India, Milko from Islamabad, Pakistan and Delgado from Bangkok. extraction.body: South Korean Police Investigate Top Tax Accountant Exam Candidate for AI Cheating South Korean authorities have launched an investigation after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using artificial intelligence to cheat. The candidate, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam, admitted via his lawyer that he photographed questions with a miniature camera, sent them to AI for answers, and viewed the results on his smartphone. This case adds to growing concerns about high-tech cheating methods, following recent incidents involving smart glasses in other certifications and upcoming plans to address similar issues in the national university entrance exam. South Korean police said Sunday they had launched an investigation after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted to using artificial intelligence to cheat. The candidate, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam held in April and July, confessed through his lawyer that he used AI to obtain answers during the tests. His score of 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, with only one wrong answer out of 160 questions, had sparked accusations that he cheated using smart glasses, which he initially denied.“We received a written confession through the test taker’s lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam,” the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency said, adding the case had been assigned to investigators. In a video posted on his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the candidate said he “deeply regretted” what he had done.“I used a miniature camera to photograph the exam questions and sent them to AI, then checked the answers on my smartphone,” he said. “I wanted to make money, and I hated seeing myself disappointing my parents after quitting a good job,” he said. The examination is administered by the Human Resources Development Service of Korea , which said two supervisors were present when the candidate sat the test.The HRDK said Sunday an “AI inspector” caught a test taker wearing smart glasses during a gas engineer certification exam last month. In October, the government announced plans to file criminal complaints against students caught using such devices in the national university entrance exam. With the annual college entrance test, known as the “Suneung”, due to take place on November 19, the presidential office said it was treating the issue seriously.The presidential office “has been working hard to come up with measures to address it,” chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun told reporters.“A meeting to discuss those measures will be held this afternoon, chaired by the presidential chief of staff for policy, and preparations are underway,” he added.

The candidate, who ranked first in both rounds of the qualification exam held in April and July, confessed through his lawyer that he used AI to obtain answers during the tests. extraction.body: For more on Jensen Huang’s resignation and the fallout from Nvidia’s leadership crisis, follow Terrence O’Brien. How it started On October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.” The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing. This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. Though, there is some disagreement among US intelligence officials over the strength of evidence tying Alice Huang to Beijing. While the paper did not confirm it at the time, rumors suggested the “close relationship” between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was romantic in nature. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair, but did not name the Megaspeed exec and alleged Chinese spy specifically. Nvidia’s board announced that it was launching an investigation into its CEO shortly after. Many believed that Jensen Huang would survive the scandal. His company’s importance to America’s booming AI industry and his crucial role at the company seemed to make him nearly untouchable. He was, after all, the only CEO the company had ever known with no clear and obvious succession plan in place, and he sat atop an unusual corporate structure with around 60 direct reports. (These numbers are slightly outdated, but according to the Harvard Business Review, 10 to 20 is far more common among Fortune 500 companies, and Tim Cook reportedly had 17 in 2015, which was deemed “a lot” by Business Insider.) Then on Wednesday, November 11th, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a second affair — this one with one of his direct reports, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Whether that was the last straw or if they were afraid it would be merely the tip of the iceberg, the board was ready to push Jensen Huang out, according to reports circulating that evening. According to Bloomberg, he had accepted his fate Wednesday evening reportedly looking “broken and shattered” and telling people, “I’m a piece of shit.” On Thursday, November 12th, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO of Nvidia. How it’s going CFO Colette Kress was immediately named interim CEO, and acknowledged to employees that this has been an “extraordinarily difficult period.” Harvey Jones was also named the first board chair in the company’s history, already signaling there would be some changes to the corporate structure. In a memo to employees, Jones said the company would “search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates.” But the destabilizing impact was immediate. Nvidia’s stock closed at an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th. It’s hard to overstate the importance of Nvidia to the US’s AI arms race with China, and the industry in general. The company has invested $99 billion in various AI labs, startups, and neo clouds. Plus has announced plans to mobilize over $500 billion in financing for building out AI data centers and other infrastructure. Even before Jensen Huang had resigned, Nvidia was already facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming the company had deceived investors. Jensen Huang and the company’s spokespeople insisted that the relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed was “completely normal and not unusual.” Only days later, Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised “national security concerns” without naming anyone specifically. According to Reuters, Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, “including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld” about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang. Many in the AI industry and Silicon Valley jumped to Jensen Huang’s defense. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a “sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” in a particularly hyperbolic post. Elon Musk said on X that it would “be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang. Many of Nvidia’s employees even voiced their support to “bring back THE boss,” on an internal post.

extraction.body: For more on Jensen Huang’s resignation and the fallout from Nvidia’s leadership crisis, follow Terrence O’Brien. How it started On October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.” The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing. This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. Though, there is some disagreement among US intelligence officials over the strength of evidence tying Alice Huang to Beijing. While the paper did not confirm it at the time, rumors suggested the “close relationship” between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was romantic in nature. On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair, but did not name the Megaspeed exec and alleged Chinese spy specifically. Nvidia’s board announced that it was launching an investigation into its CEO shortly after. Many believed that Jensen Huang would survive the scandal. His company’s importance to America’s booming AI industry and his crucial role at the company seemed to make him nearly untouchable. He was, after all, the only CEO the company had ever known with no clear and obvious succession plan in place, and he sat atop an unusual corporate structure with around 60 direct reports. (These numbers are slightly outdated, but according to the Harvard Business Review, 10 to 20 is far more common among Fortune 500 companies, and Tim Cook reportedly had 17 in 2015, which was deemed “a lot” by Business Insider.) Then on Wednesday, November 11th, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a second affair — this one with one of his direct reports, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Whether that was the last straw or if they were afraid it would be merely the tip of the iceberg, the board was ready to push Jensen Huang out, according to reports circulating that evening. According to Bloomberg, he had accepted his fate Wednesday evening reportedly looking “broken and shattered” and telling people, “I’m a piece of shit.” On Thursday, November 12th, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO of Nvidia. How it’s going CFO Colette Kress was immediately named interim CEO, and acknowledged to employees that this has been an “extraordinarily difficult period.” Harvey Jones was also named the first board chair in the company’s history, already signaling there would be some changes to the corporate structure. In a memo to employees, Jones said the company would “search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates.” But the destabilizing impact was immediate. Nvidia’s stock closed at an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th. It’s hard to overstate the importance of Nvidia to the US’s AI arms race with China, and the industry in general. The company has invested $99 billion in various AI labs, startups, and neo clouds. Plus has announced plans to mobilize over $500 billion in financing for building out AI data centers and other infrastructure. Even before Jensen Huang had resigned, Nvidia was already facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming the company had deceived investors. Jensen Huang and the company’s spokespeople insisted that the relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed was “completely normal and not unusual.” Only days later, Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised “national security concerns” without naming anyone specifically. According to Reuters, Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, “including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld” about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang. Many in the AI industry and Silicon Valley jumped to Jensen Huang’s defense. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a “sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” in a particularly hyperbolic post. Elon Musk said on X that it would “be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang. Many of Nvidia’s employees even voiced their support to “bring back THE boss,” on an internal post.

AMD is forecasting a significant uptick in growth next year and expects to sustain solid growth for a long time, driven by expansion in the server CPU market. AMD's earnings growth potential and valuation point to a nice surge in its stock price through the end of the decade. The past few months haven't been pretty for semiconductor stocks, as evidenced by the 12% decline in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector index over the past three months. Even Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) has been caught up in this vortex, experiencing significant volatility amid concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure spending, which has been key to the growth of the semiconductor sector. However, the recent weakness in the semiconductor sector has opened up a great opportunity for investors to buy a top stock at an attractive valuation. AMD is emerging as one of the most important players in the AI chip ecosystem, and I won't be surprised to see it embark on a stunning long-term rally. Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Let's see why I think that AMD could be one of the best AI stocks you can buy right now. AMD's Epyc server central processing units (CPUs) are in tremendous demand from hyperscalers and AI companies. As a result, the company's data center revenue jumped by 97% year over year in Q3 to $8.5 billion. The good news for AMD investors is that its data center segment has incredible room for growth. Alphabet 's (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google Cloud division has expanded its partnership with AMD to deploy the latter's 5th-generation Epyc server CPUs, security fabric, and x86 software to power its cloud Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) systems. AMD Epyc will serve as the foundation for Google's TPUs, allowing users to run inference applications. The good news for AMD investors is that Alphabet is poised to spend aggressively on its cloud computing infrastructure. After all, the Google Cloud business reported a backlog of a whopping $561 billion at the end of the third quarter. The tech giant expects to recognize half of that backlog in the next two years, which explains why its capital expenditure is ballooning . AMD, therefore, is going to be a direct beneficiary of Alphabet's enormous spending. Not surprisingly, the company expects its growth to accelerate at a solid clip. AMD expects revenue to increase by more than 80% in 2027, fueled by healthy growth in the data center business, where it sees the server CPU total addressable market (TAM) jump to $220 billion by 2030. Importantly, AMD is well-positioned to capitalize on this massive opportunity. It has partnerships with major hyperscalers and AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic , Meta Platforms , Microsoft , and others, in the data center segment. These customers should ensure solid long-term revenue growth for AMD, which is precisely what analysts are expecting. AMD Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts The $52.2 billion revenue estimate for 2026 points to a 51% jump over last year. The forecast for 2027 and 2028 is also quite solid, indicating that AMD is on track to become a significantly larger company. The good news for investors is that AMD's revenue growth will filter down to the bottom line as well. AMD EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts Finally, when we consider the company's long-term earnings growth potential and valuation, it becomes clear why buying this semiconductor stock amid the recent sell-off could be a smart move. AMD trades at 33 times forward earnings, making it quite attractive given the impressive pace of earnings per share (EPS) growth. It is also worth noting that analysts expect its EPS to grow by nearly 70% annually over the long run.
